note: Worked SQL queries. at_build is what each returned when the site was built, so a reader's run can disagree.

queries.title: Who is speaking, by role class
queries.note: The one classification the graph makes rather than reads, counted. `role_class` is a published formula over the listed title.
queries.sql:
SELECT role_class, COUNT(*) AS speakers
FROM nodes
WHERE type = 'Person'
GROUP BY role_class
ORDER BY speakers DESC;

queries.title: Organisations listing more than one speaker
queries.note: A join across the `listed_under` edge. Organisations are derived from the speaker cards, so this is the speaker list folded, not a registry.
queries.sql:
SELECT o.label AS organisation, COUNT(*) AS speakers
FROM edges e
JOIN nodes p ON p.id = e.source
JOIN nodes o ON o.id = e.target
WHERE e.verb = 'listed_under'
GROUP BY o.label
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY speakers DESC, organisation;

queries.title: The programme as a table
queries.note: Sessions with their stage, resolved through the `on_stage` edge. Sessions with no stage on the agenda keep NULL rather than a guess.
queries.sql:
SELECT n.day, n.time, n.label AS session, n.kind,
       (SELECT s.label FROM edges e JOIN nodes s ON s.id = e.target
        WHERE e.source = n.id AND e.verb = 'on_stage') AS stage
FROM nodes n
WHERE n.type = 'Session'
ORDER BY n.day, n.time;

queries.title: Who arrived between the two snapshots
queries.note: The `absent_from` edge is only written for people the diff found. Five names are absent from the 8 September copy and present on 13 September.
queries.sql:
SELECT p.label AS person, s.label AS snapshot, e.verb
FROM edges e
JOIN nodes p ON p.id = e.source
JOIN nodes s ON s.id = e.target
WHERE e.verb IN ('absent_from', 'present_in')
ORDER BY p.label, s.label;

queries.title: Who is no longer listed, and why the reason column is empty
queries.note: One row. The graph records the removal and never a reason, because the source gives none.

queries.title: Every verb with its inverse, in both languages
queries.note: The ontology as a table. No verb is its own inverse; that is a build gate on the Portugal section and a query here.

queries.title: The press, with the hash each page was frozen under
queries.note: Seven third-party pages, each cited only after it was frozen and hashed. The `what_it_says` column is our summary in our words; the pages are never quoted.

queries.title: What each story stands on
queries.note: The `stands_on` edge from a story to a source. A story with one publisher behind it says so here.
queries.sql:
SELECT st.label AS story, src.label AS source
FROM edges e
JOIN nodes st ON st.id = e.source
JOIN nodes src ON src.id = e.target
WHERE e.verb = 'stands_on'
ORDER BY story, source;

queries.title: A path as a sentence, the SQL way
queries.note: Session, part of, event, takes place at, place. SQL can walk a fixed-length path; it needs one join per hop and knows nothing about inverses. Compare the same question in SPARQL on the graph console.
queries.sql:
SELECT s.label AS session, 'part of' AS v1, ev.label AS event,
       'takes place at' AS v2, pl.label AS place
FROM nodes s
JOIN edges e1 ON e1.source = s.id AND e1.verb = 'part_of'
JOIN nodes ev ON ev.id = e1.target
JOIN edges e2 ON e2.source = ev.id AND e2.verb = 'takes_place_at'
JOIN nodes pl ON pl.id = e2.target
WHERE s.type = 'Session'
ORDER BY s.day, s.time
LIMIT 6;

queries.title: The most connected nodes
queries.note: Degree over both directions. The event and the two snapshots sit on top, which is what a graph built from frozen pages should look like.
queries.sql:
SELECT n.label, n.type, COUNT(*) AS degree
FROM nodes n
JOIN edges e ON e.source = n.id OR e.target = n.id
GROUP BY n.id
ORDER BY degree DESC, n.label
LIMIT 10;

queries.title: Everything within two hops of the event (recursive CTE)
queries.note: A graph traversal in SQL: a recursive common table expression walking edges in either direction, then counted by type. This is the query that shows where SQL stops being the natural language for a graph.
queries.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE hop(id, depth) AS (
  SELECT 'event:startup-summit-lisbon-2026', 0
  UNION
  SELECT CASE WHEN e.source = h.id THEN e.target ELSE e.source END, h.depth + 1
  FROM hop h JOIN edges e ON e.source = h.id OR e.target = h.id
  WHERE h.depth < 2
)
SELECT n.type, COUNT(DISTINCT n.id) AS nodes
FROM hop JOIN nodes n ON n.id = hop.id
GROUP BY n.type
ORDER BY nodes DESC;

queries.title: Unpacking a JSON column: who each story stands on, from stories.json itself
queries.note: Columns that were arrays in the JSON are stored as JSON text, and SQLite's `json_each` unpacks them. The same fact as the `stands_on` edges, read from the other file.

queries.title: The register: bytes frozen per snapshot
queries.note: Every frozen page with its size, summed by snapshot date. The bytes are the evidence; the hash in `sources.sha256` is what the build re-verifies.
queries.sql:
SELECT snapshot, COUNT(*) AS pages, SUM(bytes) AS bytes
FROM sources
GROUP BY snapshot
ORDER BY snapshot;
